entries.effect: On a named branch other than main and release-*, the version becomes <tag>+feature.<branch>.<commits since tag>.g<8-character commit hash>. The tag is the nearest reachable tag that matches v[0-9]*. If that tag does not have the form v<number>[.<number>...] with an optional -devN, -tcN or -rcN, the script prints an error and exits with code 1.
entries.name: TRON_FEATURE_BRANCH_BUILD
entries.notes: The variable has no effect on main, on release-* branches and on a detached HEAD (bin/get-version.sh:17-18). When it is on, an exact tag on HEAD is not used alone (bin/get-version.sh:30). Characters of the branch name outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot and minus become dots (bin/get-version.sh:10). The suffix -dirty is still added for a modified tree (bin/get-version.sh:47-49). bin/get-version.sh is called by bin/make-version.sh:13 (version text compiled into the binaries) and by bin/get-deb-version.sh:14 (Debian package version, which GNUmakefile:365 computes on every make run). Setters outside this area: .github/workflows/publish-deb.yml:90, bin/ci/test-get-deb-version.sh. Documented in README.ci.md:362 and packaging/tron-host/README:204. The publish workflow passes 1 on a feature branch and an empty text otherwise (bin/ci/resolve-apt-channel.sh:25-27 and .github/workflows/publish-deb.yml:90, outside this area). README.ci.md:362-365 says the script skips other v-prefixed tags. The code differs in one case: a nearest tag that matches the glob v[0-9]* but not the version form is not skipped. It stops the script with exit code 1 (bin/get-version.sh:19-27). The git and date programs that the script starts read their own variables (for example the time zone for the date part); the script text names none of them.

doc_mentions.claim: Configuration management may set TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION=1 in the shell profile of a shared development VM. The supported Make targets then use Distributed Dice without an explicit REMOTE=1. It accepts the modes 0, 1, sku0 and sku1 (lines 108-109). Make consults it for the build goals and for the test goals covered by the remote-execution policy. Format and lint goals ignore it (lines 109-111). Line 120 is an example comment.
A profile TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION=1 seeds REMOTE for the build targets as it does for the test targets.

On a shared development VM, configuration management may export TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION=1. Lines 49-50 say only test goals consult this default and that build, format and lint goals ignore it. That conflicts with doc/dice.md:109-111 and README.md:497 for build goals.
Shared development VMs may set TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION=1 in the shell profile. A command-line REMOTE value takes precedence (line 100). Line 105 repeats the precedence rule.
make test-proxy refuses to run with an inherited TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION.
Agent rule: do not set or export TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION as a routing choice.
Agent rule: never set or export TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION as a routing decision. Line 45: when a current-DUT run inherits it, use REMOTE=0.

entries.notes: The reader is GNUmakefile, outside this area. When REMOTE is not defined and the make goals include a build goal or a supported test goal, make sets REMOTE to this value (GNUmakefile:130 to GNUmakefile:133). The comment at GNUmakefile:109 says that shared development machines may set it in a shell profile. bin/bsub-build also names it. bin/slice-tests/test_dice_lsf.py sets it at 8 places. Count for the checker: the literal name is on 16 lines of the 63 files of this area (16 of them in the two test directories).

entries.effect: It supplies the remote mode when REMOTE is not defined and the goals include a build goal or a test goal from the lists at GNUmakefile:112-128. A bare 'make' counts as the goal 'all'. See REMOTE for what each mode does.
entries.name: TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION
entries.notes: It is meant for the shell profile of a shared development machine (comment at GNUmakefile:109-110). REMOTE=0 overrides it for one run. A bad value stops make with an error that names TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION (lines 145 and 159), but only when the variable is used. For other goals, such as 'make lint', the value is ignored. With the profile value 1, sku0 or sku1, a goal that runs tests directly (for example test-proxy or test-ingest) stops with the error at line 198 unless the caller adds REMOTE=0.

entries.default: /scratch/users when the variable is unset or empty.
entries.effect: Sets the root under which build directories (gen, gen-deb, gen-deb-host, gen-tsan, gen-asan, gen-coverage) are created. The checkout gets a symbolic link to <root>/<HOME relative to TRON_HOME_ROOT>/tmp/<checkout path relative to HOME>/<directory> (bin/scratch-dir.sh:25).
entries.name: TRON_SCRATCH_USERS
entries.notes: The value is also used to recognise links that point into a scratch tree (bin/scratch-dir.sh:51, bin/scratch-dir.sh:122). The script keeps a plain directory in these cases: CI is non-empty (bin/scratch-dir.sh:108); HOME is not below TRON_HOME_ROOT or the checkout is not below HOME (bin/scratch-dir.sh:24); cmake is not found or is older than 3.24 (bin/scratch-dir.sh:77-82); the target cannot be created (bin/scratch-dir.sh:160-161). The GNUmakefile runs the script when make starts (GNUmakefile:274) and from the build-directory targets (GNUmakefile:579, 636, 691, 728, 752), and it removes build directories with --remove (GNUmakefile:353), all outside this area. The comment on GNUmakefile:318-319 gives the path as /scratch/users/$USER/tmp/. The script does not read USER: the folder name is the part of HOME below TRON_HOME_ROOT (bin/scratch-dir.sh:25). bin/scratch-dir.sh:11 is the only mention of the name in the checkout, so no document describes it.
